ppcx64_exe_sha256: 0da2d0a19d9c50a1e615c3af0315ae8a2229eef34b97570bb37330761586534c
date: 2026-09-11
notes: v58 closes the one thing v57 told you it had not fixed. v57 stopped the compiler hanging on a half-written .ppu, but it only ever noticed damage it happened to trip over -- and if a unit file loses its TAIL there is nothing to trip over, because nothing an interface load reads lives in the last handful of bytes. The compiler read what it wanted, never reached the missing part, and built your program against a unit that is not all there: exit 0, no message, nothing to search a log for. Measured on a real 55291-byte unit, every truncation from 55271 bytes upward was accepted. A killed build, a full disk or an interrupted copy is exactly how a file loses its tail, so this is the same accident as v57 landing a few bytes later. The fix is the obvious comparison nobody was making: a .ppu header records how long the payload is, so a complete file is always 40 bytes of header plus that number and can never be fewer. The reader checked only that the file was big enough to hold the header, then trusted whatever followed. Now it compares the two and rejects a SHORT file; longer than declared stays legal as it always was, and the arithmetic is 64-bit so a corrupt header claiming near 4 GB cannot wrap the sum and turn the check off at the moment it is needed. THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED: if the unit's source is available the unit is recompiled and the build goes green -- measured, the .ppu comes back at full length -- and if a good copy of the same unit sits in a later -Fu directory the compiler falls through to it, also measured. Only a truncated unit with no source and no other copy stops the compile, and it stops with the message an absent unit already gives. Nobody is ever told to delete a file. The other half of the change is that the length has to BE a length: it came from Seek-to-end, which only a plain file answers with a byte count, so a .ppu read from inside a package file would have been declared truncated by exactly one byte. The length is now handed in by whoever opens the stream and knows it, and the range stream's own seek is left alone rather than bent to serve a reader that does not need it. Said plainly: no target in this compiler enables dynamic packages, so that package half cannot be exercised here and is written to be right if it is ever switched on, not proven by running it. VERIFIED: all 4000 real .ppu files in rtl/ and packages/ are exactly 40+declared bytes, so the check has no slack to fire falsely on; dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh now SCORES the tail offsets it used to document as an open gap and goes 20/25 exit 1 on the old compiler versus 25/25 exit 0 on this one, so the gate discriminates instead of describing; unit-set-loadcheck 147/147 packages load clean; full 1983-test corpus A/B against a baseline rebuilt from the same source minus the patch, 1983 SAME and 0 DIFF; self-host fixpoint stage1 == stage2 == stage3 byte-identical. WIN64 RUNTIME VERIFIED on these exact bytes under wine64 with the published v57 exe as the control: v57 accepts a unit truncated by 11, 3 and 1 bytes, v58 rejects all three, and both compile the intact unit, so the harness can still fail. The test unit sits in exactly one directory with its source off every search path, because a second copy or an available source would have let a correct rejection end in a green build and read as a pass either way. wine is NOT Windows: it runs the real shipped PE bytes through an independent reimplementation of the Win64 API, which is execution evidence for the code we generate and never a real-Windows sign-off. Nobody has yet run any VibePascal release on real Windows hardware. Compiler-binary-only refresh on v57 -- no PPU format, RTL or package change, so UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.5 MB bin alone. ppudump, ppumove and ppufiles were rebuilt because they share the reader; every other binary in bin/ is byte-identical to v57. RE-CUT once, minutes after the first v58 tarball and before anyone was told it existed: the first build reported its own build date as 2026/09/10, because FPC takes that date from when compiler/version.pas was last COMPILED and an unchanged version.pas is not recompiled just because the compiler is relinked. dist/win64-runtime-proof.sh caught it. The binary was rebuilt so it states the truth rather than the pointer being edited to agree with it; the compiler SOURCE is identical, still dedf242c69, which is why the version and the tarball name did not move. If you somehow hold a v58 bin tarball whose md5 is c74de747a8838a8cfe469a2b4bb81f41, it is that first cut -- same fix, wrong self-reported date -- and the one named above supersedes it.
